business_problem: RFDS needed to replace paper-based patient documentation and more than 100 disconnected databases with a healthcare platform that could keep working in remote areas with poor connectivity, synchronize records when links returned, and improve access to life-saving patient information across seven operating entities.
solution_summary: Royal Flying Doctor Service built its aeromedical electronic health record architecture on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using Oracle Autonomous Database for transaction processing and mixed workloads together with OCI GoldenGate replication. Clinicians in aircraft, ambulances, and remote communities capture patient interactions electronically instead of on paper, including when they are offline. Oracle Autonomous Database stores the interaction data, while OCI GoldenGate replicates and synchronizes records across RFDS systems when connectivity is restored, creating a real-time data mesh that spans remote care teams and centralized systems. By moving from CSV handoffs and standalone applications to one Oracle stack, RFDS can share patient context with hospitals and ground crews faster, support predictive diagnostics over longitudinal records, and free staff from manual administration so they spend more time on face-to-face care.
products_used: Oracle Autonomous Database for transaction processing and mixed workloads (ATP)

solution_components.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
solution_components.role: Provides the cloud foundation for RFDS's enterprisewide healthcare architecture across remote and centralized operations.

solution_components.name: Oracle Autonomous Database for transaction processing and mixed workloads (ATP)
solution_components.role: Stores patient interactions electronically and supports mixed clinical and operational workloads, including offline capture scenarios.

solution_components.name: OCI GoldenGate
solution_components.role: Replicates and synchronizes healthcare data across RFDS systems when connectivity becomes available again.

data_flow: Patient interactions are captured on digital forms in remote settings and written into Oracle Autonomous Database even when teams are offline; once connectivity returns, OCI GoldenGate synchronizes that data across RFDS systems and downstream hospital workflows so clinicians and ground crews can access current patient information quickly.
business_outcome: RFDS modernized rural care delivery with an offline-capable, zero-data-loss architecture, cut administrative work by about 30%, improved the speed and precision of emergency care handoffs, and gave clinicians more time to spend directly with patients in remote communities.
